name: F15#3: Grandpa acknowledges each current team after a real release-menu release
claim: ACCEPTANCE F15 #3 'receive Grandpa's acknowledgement of each current team, including releases' (T3: 'Grandpa recognizes each character's current companions, including releases'). Replaces the rejected f15_grandpa_acknowledges_each_team.json for the HOST half: no release is replayed and water_currents_restored is NOT ledger-set. In the Tidewake, the host (at a full five) frees the Abyssal Guardian at the chamber's real control, asks at the chamber's real invite prompt and, on the Creatures tab the game opens, lets Rill go through the REAL release menu with controller presses only (Rill's row -> ui_accept -> confirm stage -> 'Let them go' -> ui_accept -> farewell Done). The guest (with room) accepts its own Guardian through the tab's Accept. The first resolution settles the world through water_guardian_reward.gd, which is what sets water_currents_restored (asserted absent from the pre-offer world save). Both peers then cross to the Meadows through Game.enter_realm and press Grandpa's real prompt: each hears exactly its own current team named in party order, the host hears the Guardian and never Rill. DISCLOSED FIXTURES (each stands in for play that is not this criterion): (1) story_flag defeated_warden (world) stands in for the Meadows opening so Grandpa is at home rather than running the intro; (2) companions are granted by name through party_grant (the water scene boots with an empty belt; distinct names make the acknowledgement checkable); (3) guardian_fixture commits the Veilfall prerequisites and Nerissa's defeat through the ledger and injects both participants into the encounter director, whose own session path journals the reward rows (standing in for playing the Veilfall and the fight; the real-fight variant is f14_guardian_refuse_real_fight.json); (4) the Meadows crossing uses Game.enter_realm (the production crossing, not a walk to the gate); (5) grandpa_homecoming teleports each player beside Grandpa before pressing his real prompt.
